summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (96/177)

data.translation: Nun denn, so mach doch die Türe vor ihnen auf!

rationale: First p-spelled Imperativ box; same literal opening sense as the inherited Preterit.

data.turoyo: Ptəḥle l Ǧanpola u tarʕo w napiqi
data.translation: Da gab Stahlherz die Türe frei, und sie gingen hinaus.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; independent l-marked agent and zero-marked door object.

data.turoyo: Omər i naqqa d damixo i kačke, mədle la qliḏe dad dukane kulle, ptiḥile.
data.translation: Als das Mädchen eingeschlafen war, nahm er die Schlüssel aller Kammern und schloss sie auf.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; plural chamber patients indexed in ptiḥile.

data.turoyo: Ptiḥile, kito dukano ʕatəmto. I naqqa d ptəḥle i dukano ʕatəmtayo, ḥa mi taliye di dukano omər: "Ahlan wasahlan b Nari!
data.translation: Er schloss sie auf: da war eine dunkle Kammer. Als er die dunkle Kammer öffnete, sprach einer vom hinteren Ende der Kammer her: Willkommen dem Nari!

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; plural suffix followed by an overt singular chamber in the same self-contained discovery.

summary: All six occurrences retain I.1 öffnen, aufmachen; no new sense follows from opening a door versus chambers.
Ptaḥ supplies the missing Imperativ box in the p-spelled entry. Related ftḥ already has an Imperativ, so this is a local entry gap rather than an unknown opening paradigm.
Ptəḥle l Ǧanpola u tarʕo at 96/178 has an l-marked agent and a zero-marked object. ptiḥile indexes plural objects, while ptiḥoli at 96/267 appears to index a feminine object before the agent suffix.

The permitted ftḥ lookup confirms the parallel f-base and broader entry. Both p- and f- spellings occur in the same 96/267 speech; spelling variation alone does not prove separate semantics or an exclusive dialect distribution.
The complete Turoyo analysis is retained for 96/267, but its flagged German translation is not quoted because it contains substantial garbled narrative absent from the verse.
Should ptḥ remain a separate dialect entry or be cross-referenced/consolidated with ftḥ? Retain existing sense numbering and source spellings whichever editorial organisation is chosen.
Align the German for 96/267 with the source before publishing an example: the supplied translation includes material about impatient listeners and shortening absent from the Turoyo.
Confirm the object-vowel analysis of ptiḥile and ptiḥoli in the p-base paradigm, and refine the inherited mostly-southeastern distribution note using source dialect metadata.
